title: Mahavira and Nonviolence
objective: After this level you can explain how Jainism took shape around Mahavira and why Jains extend nonviolence (ahimsa) to every living thing.
summary: Jains see Mahavira, a prince turned ascetic, as the 24th and last tirthankara of this age. Because every living thing has a soul, harming any of them binds karma.

cards.headline: Would you change the way you walk to avoid stepping on an ant?
cards.body: For many Jains, the answer shapes daily life, because an ant, like every living thing, has a soul. The story starts with a prince who walked away from a palace.

cards.headline: The prince who left
cards.body: Jain tradition tells of Vardhamana, a prince who left the palace at 30 and spent twelve and a half years fasting and meditating until he reached enlightenment. He became Mahavira, "Great Hero". His traditional dates are 599 to 527 BCE, though some modern scholars place him later; he was a contemporary of the Buddha. The two main Jain branches tell some details of his life differently.

cards.headline: Not a founder, a ford builder
cards.body: Jains don't call Mahavira their founder. They believe their teachings are eternal. Mahavira is the 24th and last tirthankara of this age: a "ford builder" who shows others how to cross the currents of life. Such teachers are also called Jinas, "conquerors", because they conquered their own passions. Jains are, quite literally, followers of the conquerors.

cards.headline: A soul in every living thing
cards.body: Why such care for an ant? Jains believe every living thing has a soul, jiva. Even earth, water, fire, air and plants hold beings with one sense, touch; insects like ants have three. And harm has a cost: karma, Jains believe, is a physical substance that sticks to the soul, and harming others attracts much of it. So ahimsa, non-violence, is the heart of Jain teaching: to save your own soul, protect every other one.

cards.headline: Mahavira and Nonviolence: the takeaways
learned: Mahavira is the 24th and last tirthankara of this age
Jains believe every living thing has a soul
Harm binds karma, so ahimsa is central
